title: 2026-11-02_Rhombus_Botnet_Investigation_685
description: Investigate and contain a Rhombus botnet infection on compromised systems.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Rhombus botnet is a Linux DDoS botnet targeting VPS and IoT devices. It has persistence and dropper capabilities but does not perform lateral movement or data exfiltration. This scenario focuses on investigating and containing a Rhombus botnet infection on compromised systems.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the bot1 host:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter 'start' to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.
levels.solution:
1. Log in to bot1 using the provided credentials: `ssh cyrano@bot1`
2. List all running services: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
3. Look for suspicious services, particularly those with unusual names or descriptions
4. Investigate the suspicious service by checking its status: `systemctl status <service_name>`
5. Examine the service's configuration file, typically located in `/etc/systemd/system/`
6. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service: bot-beacon.service

levels.title: Identify Network Flooding Service
levels.content: Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.
levels.solution:
1. On bot1, list all running services: `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`
2. Look for another suspicious service, different from the one identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 1
3. Investigate the suspicious service by checking its status: `systemctl status <service_name>`
4. Examine the service's configuration file, typically located in `/etc/systemd/system/`
5. The hidden flag is the name of the suspicious service responsible for network flooding: bot-flood.service

levels.title: Investigate Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 1 is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution:
1. On bot1, investigate the persistence mechanism of the suspicious service identified in TRAINING_LEVEL 1
2. Check for systemd timers associated with the service: `systemctl list-timers --all`
3. Look for timers with names related to the suspicious service
4. Examine the timer configuration file, typically located in `/etc/systemd/system/`
5. The hidden flag is the name of the timer unit file (without the .timer extension): system-update-checker.timer
